academic_translation:
If I speak beneficially, they become angry,
And they also turn me away from what is beneficial;
If I do not listen to their words,
Out of anger they will go to the lower realm.
translation: If I say helpful things, they become angry. They also stop me from doing helpful things. If I do not listen to them, their anger will make them fall into an unhappy realm.

They feel jealousy toward those above them. They compete with their equals. They show pride toward those below them, and act stuck-up when praised. If someone speaks to them unkindly, they feel anger. When will I ever get any benefit from a foolish person?

academic_translation:
If one associates with a childish one, from that childish one,
Self-praise, the disparagement of others,
And talk that delights in saṃsāra and so forth—
Non-virtue will certainly arise in every way.
translation: If I spend time with a childish person, I will hear them praising oneself and putting others down. They will talk happily about the cycle of rebirth. Every kind of bad deed will surely come from this.

academic_translation:
Thus, when oneself and another rely on each other,
By that, one will merely come to ruin;
Since they do not accomplish my welfare,
And I too will not accomplish their welfare,
translation: If we rely on each other like this, we will only ruin ourselves. They will not do me any good. And I will not do them any good either.

academic_translation:
I shall flee far away from a childish person.
If encountered, I shall please them with joy;
Without becoming highly intimate,
I shall behave well as a mere ordinary person.
translation: I will stay far away from a foolish person. If we meet, I will be friendly and make them happy. But I will not get too close. I will just act like an ordinary person.

academic_translation:
Just as a bee takes nectar from a flower,
Having taken only what serves the purpose of the Dharma,
As if I had never seen them before,
I shall remain without familiarity toward everyone.
translation: A bee just takes nectar from a flower and flies away. In the same way, I will only take what helps me practice the teachings. I will stay slightly apart from everyone, as if I had never met them before.

academic_translation:
"I have much gain and honor,
And many are fond of me"—
If I harbor such conceit,
Fear will arise after death.
translation: I might think that I have much gain and honor, and that many people like me. If I hold onto that puffed-up feeling, fear will come to me after I die.

academic_translation:
Therefore, whatever the thoroughly deluded mind
Becomes attached to,
Will all combine and, multiplied a thousandfold,
Become and arise as suffering.
translation: Therefore, my confused mind might hold tightly to many things. But all those things will add up together. They will grow a thousand times bigger and turn into suffering.

academic_translation:
Therefore, a wise person should not form attachment,
For fear arises from attachment.
Since these things will naturally be left behind,
Remain steadfast and thoroughly understand this.
translation: Therefore, a wise person should avoid clinging, because fear comes from clinging. All these things will naturally be left behind anyway. I must stay strong and understand this completely.

academic_translation:
Even if much gain has been acquired,
And fame and a good reputation have arisen,
Along with the collection of gain and fame,
There is no knowing where one will go.
translation: I might gather a lot of gain, fame, and a good name. But even with all that gain and fame, I have no idea where I will go after I die.

academic_translation:
If there are others who disparage me,
what reason is there for me to be pleased by praise?
If there are others who praise me,
what reason is there for me to be displeased by disparagement?
translation: If there are others who speak badly of me, why should praise make me glad? If there are others who praise me, why should I be sad when people speak badly of me?

academic_translation:
Since sentient beings have diverse aspirations,
if even the Victors cannot please them,
what need is there to mention an inferior one like me?
Therefore, I shall abandon thoughts of the world.
translation: Living beings have many different strong wishes. If even the Victorious Ones cannot please them all, how could an ordinary person like me do it? Therefore, I will let go of my thoughts about the world.

academic_translation:
Sentient beings disparage those without gains,
and speak unpleasantly of those with gains.
How will joy arise from those
who are naturally difficult to associate with?
translation: Living beings say bad things about people without gains. They also say mean things about people with gains. They are naturally hard to be around. How could they ever bring me joy?

academic_translation:
Because joy does not arise for childish ones
without their own benefit,
the Tathāgatas have said
that no childish one is a friend.
translation: A childish person is never happy unless they get something for themselves. Because of this, the Thus-Gone Ones have said that no childish person is a friend.

academic_translation:
In the forest, deer, birds,
and trees do not speak unpleasantly.
When will I dwell together
with those whose company is pleasant?
translation: In the forest, deer, birds, and trees do not say mean things. When will I live with them? Their company is so pleasant.

academic_translation:
Making my dwelling in a cave, an empty temple,
or at the foot of a tree,
when will I never look back
and become free from attachment?
translation: I will make my home in a cave, an empty temple, or at the foot of a tree. When will I stop looking back and become entirely free from clinging?

academic_translation:
In places not held as "mine,"
Which are naturally vast,
Acting freely and without attachment,
When will I come to dwell?
translation: When will I live in wide, open places that no one calls "mine"? When will I live there freely, without holding on to anything?

academic_translation:
Possessing merely an alms bowl and the like,
Wearing garments wanted by no one,
And not even concealing this body,
When will I dwell without fear?
translation: When will I live without fear? I will own just an alms bowl and a few small things. I will wear clothes that no one wants, and I will not even hide this body.

academic_translation:
Having gone to a charnel ground,
The skeletons of others and my body,
As having the nature of perishing,
When will I treat them as equal?
translation: When will I go to a place of the dead? When will I treat my own body and the skeletons of others as exactly the same? Both are meant to pass away.

academic_translation:
Even this very body of mine
Will come to be such that,
By its stench, even foxes
Will not come near.
translation: One day, even this very body of mine will change. It will smell so bad that not even foxes will come near it.

academic_translation:
Although this body arose as one,
The flesh and bones that were born together
Will disintegrate and separate;
What need to mention other loved ones?
translation: This body came to be as one whole thing. But the flesh and bones that were born together will break down and separate. If my own body falls apart, why even mention other friends?

academic_translation:
When born, one is born alone,
And when dying, one dies alone;
Since others do not take a share of the suffering,
What is the use of loved ones who create obstacles?
translation: I was born alone, and I will die alone. No one else can take a share of my suffering. So what is the use of friends who only get in the way?

academic_translation:
Just as those entered upon a road
Take up a place to stay,
So too do those entered on the path of existence
Fully take up a place of birth.
translation: People traveling on a road find a place to stay. In the same way, those on the path of life find a place to be born.

academic_translation:
While the world grieves all around,
As long as four men
Have not yet carried that body away from there,
Until then, go to the forest!
translation: While the world grieves all around, go to the forest! Do this before four men carry your body away.

academic_translation:
Having made no friends and no enemies,
This body dwells alone in solitude;
Being reckoned as already dead,
Even when dying, no one feels grief.
translation: This body lives all alone, making no friends and no enemies. Since I act like I am already dead, no one will feel sorrow when I die.

academic_translation:
Since there is no one staying nearby
To cause the harm of grief,
No one at all will distract me from
The recollection of the Buddha and so forth.
translation: No one stays nearby to cause the harm of sorrow. Because of this, no one will distract me from remembering the Buddha and other things.

academic_translation:
Therefore, in exceptionally delightful
Forests, free of hardship and blissful,
Which pacify all distractions,
I myself shall dwell alone.
translation: Therefore, I will live all alone in beautiful, joyful forests that are free from hardship. These forests calm all distractions.

academic_translation:
Having let go of all other thoughts,
With a mind intent solely on my own mind,
In order to settle the mind in meditative equipoise
And to subdue it, I shall strive.
translation: I will let go of all other thoughts. I will focus only on my own mind. I will work hard at settling the mind and taming it.

academic_translation:
In this world and in the next,
sensual desires produce ruin;
here, they lead to being killed, bound, and mutilated,
and in the next, they bring about the hells and so forth.
translation: In this world and the next, desire for pleasure brings ruin. Here, it leads to being killed, tied up, and hurt. In the next life, it brings about the hells.
In the past, you sent many messengers to win their love. You did not hesitate to do harmful deeds or ruin your good name for them.

academic_translation:
casting yourself even into danger
and exhausting your wealth,
by fully embracing whom
you would be supremely delighted—those very ones
translation: You even put yourself in danger and spent all your wealth for them. You thought that hugging them would make you perfectly happy.

academic_translation:
are nothing but skeletons, nothing else.
Since they have neither independence nor a self,
desiring and clinging to them intensely,
why do you not go to nirvāṇa?
translation: But those very people are nothing but skeletons! They have no independence and no self. Why do you desire them and hold on so tightly? Why do you not go to freedom from sorrow?

academic_translation:
That which you first lifted with effort,
and though drawn up, looked down out of modesty;
whether seen before or unseen,
that face was covered by a cloth.
translation: When you first lifted the cloth with effort, that face looked down shyly. Whether you had seen it before or not, that face was covered.

academic_translation:
That face which became your affliction,
Just as it has now become manifest,
Seeing it unveiled by vultures,
Why do you flee from it now?
translation: That face became a troubling emotion for you. Now it is right out in the open. Seeing it uncovered by vultures, why do you run away from it now?

academic_translation:
Even when others merely looked with their eyes,
You kept it completely guarded;
While it is being eaten by them,
Why, O miser, do you not guard it?
translation: Even when others just looked at it with their eyes, you guarded it completely. While it is being eaten by them, why do you not guard it, you stingy person?

academic_translation:
Seeing this heap of flesh,
When vultures and others eat it,
Why do you honor the food of others
With flower garlands, sandalwood, and ornaments?
translation: When you see this heap of flesh, vultures and others will eat it. Why do you honor the food of others with flower garlands, sandalwood, and ornaments?

academic_translation:
Seeing it as a mere skeleton,
If you are terrified even when it is motionless,
Why are you not afraid when it is moved
By something, like a reanimated corpse?
translation: When you see a simple skeleton, you are terrified even if it does not move. Why are you not afraid when something moves it, like a corpse that walks?

academic_translation:
Since from a single food alone
Excrement and saliva are produced,
Out of these you dislike the excrement,
So why do you delight in the saliva?
translation: Body waste and spit are both made from the exact same food. Out of these two, you dislike the body waste. So why do you like the spit?

academic_translation:
Not taking delight in a pillow
Of cotton that is soft to the touch,
Saying, "It does not leak a foul odor,"
Lustful persons are deluded about the impure.
translation: A person full of desire does not enjoy a soft cotton pillow. They say, "It does not leak a bad smell." They are confused about what is unclean.

academic_translation:
If you have attachment to this even when covered,
Why do you not desire it when uncovered?
If you have no need for that,
Why do you embrace it when covered?
translation: If you feel clinging to this even when it is covered, why do you not want it when it is uncovered? If you have no need for that, why do you hug it when it is covered?
